title: Phone Cycle
description:
Status: In development — website and CMS are largely completed



PhoneCycle is a fully custom-built web application developed as a freelance project, allowing consumers to sell their used smartphones to PhoneCycle. The platform consists of two parts: a public-facing website for customers and an internal CMS for staff.



Public website: Customers go through a step-by-step questionnaire (brand, model, storage capacity, screen condition, back cover, housing, and battery percentage), based on which a price is automatically calculated. After accepting the offer, they choose between dropping off the device or receiving a shipping label, fill in their personal details, and their submission is processed. PostNL integration for shipping labels is currently pending client input.



CMS (admin panel): Staff log in via JWT authentication and have access to a submission overview with status management, tracking each device from registration through to payment or return. Each submission has its own detail page with a full status history and the ability to add internal notes. The panel also includes device management for creating and toggling brands, models, and storage options, as well as a pricing module where staff can configure prices per device and condition.
technical-description: Built with Vue 3, TypeScript, Pinia and Vite on the frontend, and NestJS with Prisma ORM and PostgreSQL on the backend. Additional integrations include JWT authentication, SendGrid for email, the PostNL API for shipping labels, and Docker for deployment.

title: Social Care Companion Node
description:
For this school/minor project (Smart Cities), we developed a smart care companion system for elderly people. The platform consists of four interconnected components: a web-based
  CMS for administrators and caregivers, a REST API backend, a Wear OS app for smartwatches, and firmware for a Raspberry Pi IoT device deployed at the patient's home.

  The web application serves two distinct audiences. The CMS (for admins and caregivers) allows managing patients and caregivers, viewing health statistics, and handling care
  relations. The companion view is a patient-facing dashboard designed to run on a screen at the patient's home — it greets the patient by name, shows the current time and date,
  indoor temperature and humidity measured by the Raspberry Pi, live outdoor weather, the daily agenda, and a button to directly call their caregiver. Patients can also make voice
  recordings through the interface.

  Health data — heart rate and daily step count — is collected from a paired Wear OS smartwatch and surfaced in both the CMS and the patient dashboard.

  As the lead on both frontend and backend, I built the Angular web application and the NestJS API from the ground up — including JWT-based authentication with role-based access
  control (Admin, Caregiver, Patient), a layered repository/service/controller architecture, and a full Swagger API reference.
technical-description: Built with Angular (web), NestJS + Prisma + PostgreSQL (API), Wear OS (Android smartwatch), and MicroPython on an ESP32-C3 (Raspberry Pi IoT device). Deployed with Docker Compose.

title: Smart Heaven
description:
For this school/minor project, we were tasked with building a smart city simulation where physical embedded devices — such as traffic lights, railway barriers, and parking sensors — communicate with a
  central management platform. The goal was to demonstrate how IoT devices in a smart city can be monitored and controlled in real time.
  
  Since I already had experience with web development and API design, I took on the responsibility for both the frontend dashboard (web) and the backend API. The API handles device registration, telemetry
  ingestion from embedded hardware, live state tracking, logging, and user management. The dashboard gives operators an overview of all connected devices, hardware types, statuses, and logs.

title: Visie op de uitslag
description:
For this school project, we developed a platform to visualize statistics from the 2023 elections. In addition to the statistics, we also built a forum where users can engage in discussions — inspired by platforms like Reddit and Stack Overflow. The project was developed by a team of four students using Spring Boot (API) and Vue.js (frontend).

We also created a CMS system for managing the forum content. Visitors can log in using the credentials email: admin@admin.com and password: admin to explore the CMS. Please note that not all features are fully functional yet, as this was a prototype built within a limited time frame
technical-description: Built with vue.js (website) and Spring Boot (API)

title: VR Balance
description:
For this school/minor project, we were tasked with developing a VR application in Unity to help users improve their balance and reduce lower back pain. Additionally, the client requested a CMS platform to manage users and view patient statistics.

Since I already had experience with web development and data handling, I took on the responsibility for both the frontend (website) and backend (API) of the system. Visitors can log in using the credentials email: admin@vrbalance.com and password: admin to explore the CMS.
technical-description: Built with vue.js (website), Unity (VR-app) and Spring Boot (API)
